kept.title: Zip Slip Path Traversal
kept.description: The library allows extraction of files without adequate path validation. While some methods attempt sanitization, the `extractAllTo` function uses `canonical` and `sanitize` which rely on user-controlled zip entry names, potentially allowing writing files outside the intended target directory.
steps_to_exploit: Create a malicious zip file containing an entry named '../../../../tmp/evil.sh'.
Call extractAllTo on the zip file with a target path.
The library resolves the path to a location outside the target folder, overwriting arbitrary files on the system.
kept.impact: Remote Code Execution or Arbitrary File Overwrite on the host system running the library.

kept.title: Use of Weak ZipCrypto Algorithm
kept.description: The library implements ZipCrypto, which is cryptographically broken and vulnerable to known-plaintext attacks, enabling password recovery.
steps_to_exploit: Obtain an encrypted zip file using ZipCrypto.
Obtain at least 12 bytes of known plaintext (e.g., a file header).
Use automated tools to recover the session keys and decrypt the file content without the password.
kept.impact: Complete compromise of confidentiality for encrypted zip archives.

kept.title: Potential Arbitrary Code Execution via Unsafe `randomFillSync`
kept.description: The library attempts to generate random salts for ZipCrypto using `Math.random` as a fallback if `randomFillSync` is not available, leading to predictable salt generation in certain environments.
steps_to_exploit: Run the library in a restricted environment where `crypto` module is unavailable or broken.
Predict salt values generated by the weak `Math.random` implementation.
Use predicted salts to bypass security or guess keys.
kept.impact: Weakening of cryptographic protections due to predictable entropy.

kept.title: Insecure File Permissions Handling
kept.description: The library explicitly sets file permissions to 0666 or uses modes from the zip archive during extraction, potentially exposing sensitive files to other users on the system.
steps_to_exploit: Construct a zip archive with files configured with insecure Unix permissions (e.g., 0777).
Extract these files using the library in a multi-user environment.
The library writes files with permissive modes, granting read/write access to other local users.
kept.impact: Unauthorized access to extracted data by other local users.

kept.title: Prototype Pollution / Incorrect Merging
kept.description: The use of `Object.assign` with `Object.create(null)` for options without recursive checks or property filtering makes the library susceptible to prototype pollution if external input is passed directly to the constructor.
steps_to_exploit: Pass a malicious object as an option to the AdmZip constructor containing a `__proto__` property.
The `Object.assign` call merges this property into the base options object.
The application logic behavior is modified due to the polluted prototype.
kept.impact: Modification of application behavior or potential security bypasses.

kept.title: Synchronous Blocking I/O in Async API
kept.description: The `extractAllToAsync` function performs synchronous directory creation and file system operations within its logic, which can block the Node.js event loop.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an extraction of a large zip archive.
The library calls `filetools.makeDir` or other sync methods during the async process.
The Node.js event loop is blocked, preventing the server from handling other concurrent requests.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) due to event loop exhaustion.

kept.title: Lack of Memory Limits on Decompression
kept.description: When decompressing, the library allocates a buffer based on the `size` field in the central header without verifying if the available system memory is sufficient, leading to potential out-of-memory errors.
steps_to_exploit: Create a zip archive with an entry reporting an extremely large `size` (e.g., several GBs).
Call the decompression method on that entry.
The library attempts to allocate the requested size in RAM, crashing the process.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via memory exhaustion.

kept.title: Use of unsafe `parseInt` in compression
kept.description: The deflater uses `parseInt` on the buffer length for chunk calculation, which may lead to incorrect chunk sizes if the input length is not an integer or is very large.
steps_to_exploit: Provide a very large or specifically crafted Buffer as input to the deflater.
The chunk size calculation results in invalid parameters for `zlib.deflateRawSync`.
Possible unexpected behavior during compression.
kept.impact: Instability or potential data corruption during compression.

kept.title: Insecure Recursive Directory Traversal
kept.description: The `findFilesAsync` method recursively reads directories without depth limiting, susceptible to stack overflow if directory nesting is extremely deep.
steps_to_exploit: Create a file system directory structure with extremely deep nesting.
Call `findFilesAsync` on the root of this structure.
The recursion exceeds the stack size, causing the application to crash.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) via stack overflow.

kept.title: Implicit Trust in Zip Header Metadata
kept.description: The library relies heavily on metadata provided within the zip file (like `size` and `compressedSize`) to perform memory allocations and file operations without secondary verification.
steps_to_exploit: Craft a zip file with conflicting header information (e.g., local header size vs central directory size).
The library may attempt to read past buffer bounds or allocate incorrect memory blocks during extraction.
Potential for buffer overflow or out-of-bounds read vulnerabilities in underlying Node.js calls.
kept.impact: Potential memory corruption or process crash.

kept.title: Incomplete Path Sanitization in `sanitize`
kept.description: The `sanitize` function iterates through parts of a path and joins them. If a path contains complex combinations of separators, it might return a path that escapes the intended root prefix.
steps_to_exploit: Create a filename with a sequence of separators and parent references that bypass the `startsWith(prefix + pth.sep)` check.
Trigger extraction to a directory, causing the file to be written to a restricted location.
kept.impact: File system injection/traversal leading to arbitrary file write.

kept.title: Unsafe `Buffer.fill(0)` on potential user input
kept.description: The library fills buffers with zeros but does not clear them securely when handling sensitive data like passwords or decrypted keys, potentially leaving residues in memory.
steps_to_exploit: Perform a memory dump of the Node.js process after a zip operation involving passwords.
Identify sensitive data residues (passwords/keys) that were not zeroed out.
Extract sensitive information from memory.

kept.title: Missing Error Handling in `writeZip`
kept.description: The `writeZip` function silences errors when writing data to disk, making it impossible for the calling code to know if the zip file was actually saved correctly.
steps_to_exploit: Call `writeZip` on a path where the user has no write permission.
The library fails silently or returns an incorrect status.
The user assumes the zip file is updated when it is not.
kept.impact: Data loss or inconsistent application state.

kept.title: Potential DOS via Regex in `addLocalFolderAsync2`
kept.description: The library allows passing user-defined RegEx filters for folder processing, which can lead to Regular Expression Denial of Service (ReDoS).
steps_to_exploit: Pass a maliciously crafted regular expression that is computationally expensive to evaluate.
Call `addLocalFolderAsync2` on a large directory structure.
The CPU usage spikes due to back-tracking, causing a denial of service.
kept.impact: Denial of Service (DoS) through CPU exhaustion.

kept.title: Insecure usage of `process.nextTick` for control flow
kept.description: The `nextTick` usage in `addLocalFolderAsync` can potentially starve the I/O event loop if the file list is large, preventing other I/O operations.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger large folder processing using `addLocalFolderAsync`.
The recursion via `nextTick` floods the queue.
Other pending I/O operations are blocked, affecting system responsiveness.
